key_insight: In metal-halide perovskites, localized carrier spin relaxation is dominated by hyperfine coupling, with electrons mainly interacting with halogen nuclei and holes with metal nuclei, requiring an exact dynamical model instead of a simple exponential decay.
engineering_relevance: Understanding which atomic species control spin lifetimes can guide perovskite composition choices to improve carrier coherence and inform spintronic and optoelectronic device design.
method: Adapted a muon-spin-relaxation model to localized carrier spins
Solved longitudinal spin relaxation exactly across arbitrary hyperfine correlation times
Fit time-resolved Faraday rotation data to extract localization volume and correlation time
evidence_signal: The abstract reports application to time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two perovskite samples, where the exact model outperformed a single-exponential approximation and enabled parameter extraction.
watch_item: The framework is for localized carriers and its conclusions may not directly transfer to delocalized transport states or compositions outside the measured regime.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
